themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 215 THIS WEEK, up 292% from the 8-week baseline average of 54.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.58), suggesting a rapid deterioration in road quality across Jamaica/Hollis/St. Albans that may reflect winter damage, deferred maintenance, or a sudden reporting surge worth investigating.
evidence: 215 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 54.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (+292%)
Z-score of 5.58 indicates statistically significant spike
Long-standing community board budget request for sidewalk/curb/pedestrian ramp repairs suggests chronic baseline problem now accelerating
reporting_angles: Map the geographic hot spots of complaints within CD412 to determine if this is citywide winter damage or localized infrastructure failure
Interview DOT about current repair capacity and timeline; cross-check with street maintenance schedules filed with the city

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Failure
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK, a 1000% spike from the 8-week baseline of 1.0 complaint per week (z-score: 10.0), pointing to either a sudden sanitation service collapse or a concentrated problem area residents are newly mobilizing to report.
evidence: 11 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (+1000%)
Z-score of 10.0 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Community board has standing request for more on-street trash cans and recycling containers (DSNY), suggesting systemic cleanliness concerns
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if there was a service disruption, staffing issue, or schedule change this week in CD412
Geolocate the 11 complaints to see if they cluster in one neighborhood (Jamaica vs. Hollis vs. St. Albans) or are dispersed

themes_detail.label: Animal Sanitation & Park Rule Violations
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about unsanitary animal conditions on private property spiked 167% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 1.1 baseline, z-score: 5.67), and park rule violations exploded 2300% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.1 baseline, z-score: 8.69), suggesting either a new nuisance hot spot or emerging enforcement gap in CD412's parks and residential areas.
evidence: Unsanitary animal (private property) complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (+167%, z-score: 5.67)
Park rule violations: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (+2300%, z-score: 8.69)
Community board requests for park maintenance and safety are recurring budget asks, indicating historic concern
reporting_angles: Identify the specific parks and addresses where rule violations and animal nuisances are clustering
Interview Parks Department about enforcement patrols and animal control response times in CD412

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, up 700% from the 8-week baseline of 0.4 complaints weekly (z-score: 5.42), potentially signaling vacant properties, illegal dumping, or deferred maintenance becoming visible and reportable problems.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (+700%)
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant spike
DOB data shows 767 total permit filings in last 90 days, but high alteration/low new construction (533 alt vs. 114 new) may indicate aging housing stock
reporting_angles: Map the three reported lots to determine if they are connected (same owner, same block, same development zone)
Cross-reference with DOB and HPD databases to identify whether these are abandoned properties, code violations, or properties in foreclosure

themes_detail.label: Wood Pile Violation Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Wood pile remaining complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, up 2300% from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 complaints weekly (z-score: 8.69), potentially indicating illegal construction debris dumping, contractor violations, or a single major site creating multiple complaints.
evidence: 3 wood pile remaining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (+2300%)
114 new building permits filed in last 90 days provide context for potential construction debris issues
reporting_angles: Geolocate the three wood pile complaints to determine if they stem from one active construction site or multiple violations
Contact DSNY Enforcement and DOB to identify whether permits exist for the sites and whether fines have been issued
